Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust's : Sebokeng Paediatric Trauma Unit

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight on Carte Blanche, we spotlight a vital mission: the creation of Sebokeng Hospital's first pediatric trauma unit, a safe haven for children in crisis.

Unique Selling Point:
This episode highlights not just the consistency and dedication of the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust but also the resilience required to face down threats from the construction mafia, determined to derail this life-saving project.

Summary:
The need for specialized pediatric trauma care in South Africa is critical, especially in emergency departments where children are treated alongside adults, often exacerbating their trauma. At Sebokeng Hospital, Dr. Teletsane, Head of Paediatrics, had taken it upon himself to create a makeshift space for children in need of urgent care. However, the hospital lacked a dedicated facility for pediatric emergencies, which is where the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust steps in.

This episode will explore the journey of transforming pediatric care at Sebokeng Hospital through the construction of a specialized trauma unit. We'll follow the story from the cramped, temporary unit where children had treated to the new facility, now near completion , thanks to the Trust and its partners. We'll delve into the unique challenges of building a hospital, including the innovative design and the specialized team behind it.

Further information:
However, the journey hasn't been without obstacles. The construction mafia, notorious for disrupting projects across South Africa, has threatened to derail this vital build. Despite these threats, the Trust and the construction team have remained steadfast, committed to ensuring that Sebokeng's children receive the care they desperately need.

This episode will include interviews with Dr. Teletsane, the Trust's representatives, and the construction team, providing insight into the broader impact of this project. We'll also highlight the Trust's consistent work over the years

Script:


CMADT : Sebokeng


1.V/O It's Tuesday morning, barely light and for Roland Marsh, there's no time to lose— he’s driven by the urgency of the day ahead.

2.V/O He's a crucial part of a team racing against time, with just three months left to complete South Africa's first dedicated paediatric trauma unit at Sebokeng Regional Hospital, south of Gauteng.

Upsound Roland Marsh[site walk about in the morning] : 00:05 This is what I call a milestone where you get to build something as awesome as this for a kid that you don't know. [transition/fade out]

3.V/O Over the past decade, the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust has built two pediatric high-care wards at Sebokeng Hospital, but these wards are now stretched beyond capacity, serving 1.3 million people in the Sedibeng region.

Upsound old story January 2024 : 01 :39 Dr Theletsane: We don’t have an ICU. We should get a child, stabilize the child, and then look for space in a tertiary centre Dr Theletsane// Because the ICUs are almost always full, we are forced to be stuck with a child where we have to do everything.

4.V/O Recognizing the critical need, the Trust launched its third and most ambitious project at the hospital: a pioneering paediatric trauma unit.

Link: … It's been about 5 months since we checked up on progress on this incredible construction behind me. It's a state of the art , one of a kind trauma unit, a project like this however does come with its ups and downs.

5.V/O The pediatric unit is now 80% finished and still bustling with activity.

[breather]


6 V/O BUT The build encountered many unexpected obstacles before reaching this point. Soil conditions forced design changes, straining the tight budget. Quantity Surveyor Frits Relling was crucial in keeping the project on track financially.

Fritz Relling 01:23 Initially we're going to do a double story, but after re-engineering and recasting , we had a few curveballs from then on. We had very bad ground conditions, so we had to do raft foundations, expensive foundations.

VO.Billy Neethling, the appointed building contractor overseeing this project, faced a complex challenge. Nestled between existing hospital buildings, the construction of the new pediatric unit required the team to work with precision to avoid disrupting critical life-saving functions.

Upsound Billy Neethling 26:16 You can't shut down the hospital and say, okay, fine, you won't need water or medical gas for the next two hours.

Upsound Billy Neethling 26:46 once we cut into the pipes, the lines there, we've got to put in temporary feeds in a lot of the wards in the line of gas bottles, medical gas bottles, and get them connected in, get them checked at the 100%, pressurized, everything. And then only can we work on the gas lines.27:14


V/O More was still to come

.Link :Sebokeng Hospital was opened back in 1983. The people, the staff are willing. The buildings and facilities, however, are a relic of the past. And what this build seeks to do is to take us into the future. But there are always those who are willing to thwart progress in pursuit of profit.

.V/O In February this year , The Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust faced its most formidable obstacle yet: safeguarding the construction team from the looming threat of the local Construction Mafia.

V/O Carte Blanche has reported on similar intimidation tactics before.

V/O Masquerading as "business forums," these organized criminal groups violently disrupt construction projects, extorting money, jobs, and control through intimidation, vandalism, and violence…And now they wanted a piece of this project funded entirely by donors


Upsound Roland08:07 They do come in groups of three, four people at a time.trying to intimidate us

Upsound Billy 03:36 They came in, and , they now demand that they get to work.


[tension/breather]

Upsound Billy 04:01….and then things started really getting heated up.

Upsound Billy 02:28 Then I started getting some nasty , SMSs. would start on a Friday and run through to a Sunday evening.

12.V/O Billy lived in constant fear. The threat was imminent, forcing him to be hypervigilant.

Upsound bily 17:13 : it was scary. Every time I drive here, you drive with a sense of who's behind you, who's in front of you, who's next to you. 17:36If I see a car pull up, I check if their windows are open, or if it's a taxi, whether the door's gonna slide open

13. V/O Patron of the Trust Karolina Andropoulos, had to make a tough choice.
Upsound Karolina 06:59There was a day where I felt real fear. I'd called everyone off construction and halted construction. And thought that we, t, really needed to handle the security situation primarily for the safety of the workers on site.

14. V/O After halting construction, the trust, hospital management and staff, secured a protection order against the suspected leader of the Sebokeng construction mafia. This seemed to send a message that the Trust meant business and Finally, work could resume.

14Upsound Xola 14:16 You must be really happy to be able to stand back and think, almost there. [Billy]Yeah, no, it is, and it's a great feeling.


Upsound Billy 14:46 It's a team effort. And if it wasn't for the team, we wouldn't be standing here. I mean, it's from the architects to the QS of the engineers, my building team, the local involvement that we got from the locals working on site.5:04 the hospital staff, everybody. It was just a massive team effort and yeah, eventually we're standing here and it's on its way to completion


Frits Relling 01:35 . we're nearly into budget and very proud of what's happening here.
[breather / ominous tone/music]


15. V/O Before welcoming our smallest patients, Sakhiwo's clinical engineer, Antionette Boshoff, will finalize the unit by ensuring all medical equipment is in the right place and in perfect working order.

Upsound Antionette Boshoff [ walk and talk interview] : we basically do all the HT equipment for the project, so that's the health technology.. It includes medical equipment, as well as furniture fittings, trolleys and consumables.

[ Xola]So you can paint a picture for us?

Upsound Antionette Boshoff Yes, we basically just round off the whole facility so that it actually becomes a medical facility. And not just the building.

[Xola]You give it life? Yes.

[breather/transition ]

16. V/O For Head of Paediatrics Dr .Thaphehlo Theletsane the Trauma unit can’t come soon enough.


Upsound Dr Theletsane 03:27 all of us as a team are extremely excited about it. And we've never seen something like this anywhere in South Africa. And hopefully, this beautiful building will actually change the face of South Africa
[breather]

Upsound Roland [Interview] 14:38 I take a huge amount of pride in what I do. I like to stand back and admire what I was doing. That is the only thing driving me at the moment. That's... This is my passion. I


[emotive music to end off]
—-- end —--
